What is the fastest way to enumerate all subdomains of a target domain?

Use a multi-tool pipeline: amass enum -d target.com -passive for passive, subfinder -d target.com for fast API-based enumeration, then assetfinder --subs-only target.com. Feed all results into dnsx for live resolution: cat all_subs.txt | dnsx -silent. Cross-reference with certificate transparency logs via crt.sh: curl -s 'https://crt.sh/?q=%.target.com&output=json' | jq -r '.[].name_value' | sort -u. For deeper results combine with gobuster dns -d target.com -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/deepmagic.com-prefixes-top50000.txt.

How does Shodan work and what can you extract from it?

Shodan continuously scans the entire internet on all ports and stores banner data, SSL certificates, and service fingerprints. Key searches: org:'Target Corp' to find all IPs in their ASN, hostname:target.com for all indexed subdomains, ssl.cert.subject.cn:target.com for all SSL certificates, port:22 country:US for SSH servers. Use Shodan Dorks: 'default password' title:'DVR Login', http.favicon.hash:<hash> to find instances of specific software. API usage: shodan search 'org:Target' --fields ip_str,port,org,hostnames. Shodan reveals: open ports, software versions, default creds, ICS/SCADA systems, webcams, VPNs. Supplement with Censys (more thorough SSL/TLS data) and FOFA for Chinese/Asian infrastructure.

Explain how to conduct GEOINT from a single photo.

Start with metadata: exiftool photo.jpg extracts GPS coordinates if not stripped. If no GPS: analyze scene elements — vegetation type narrows climate zone, road signs narrow country/region, architecture style narrows era and region, sun angle + shadows give time of day and hemisphere. Tools: GeoSpy.ai for automated ML-based geolocation, GeoGuessr community for manual analysis. Search visible text (signs, labels) in Google Street View. Cross-reference sky/weather patterns with historical weather data for a specific date. Check image background for unique landmarks queryable in Wikimapia or Google Earth. Use PanTool or Google Earth Pro to match satellite imagery. For social media: download image and check upload timestamp vs account activity for timezone correlation.

What is SOCMINT and what are the best tools for it?

SOCMINT (Social Media Intelligence) is collecting intelligence from social platforms. Best tools: Maigret — searches 300+ platforms for a username, generates detailed profile report. Blackbird — fast username enumeration with detailed output. Sherlock — 300+ site checks. Social-Analyzer — profiles across platforms with risk scoring. SNSCRAPE — scrapes Twitter/Reddit/Instagram without API limits (bypasses rate limiting). Tinfoleak — deep Twitter OSINT (tweets, locations, devices, hashtags). For Facebook: graph.tips and lookup-id.com. For Instagram: Instadp for profile picture download, Storysaver for stories. For LinkedIn: LinkedInt, proxycurl API. Walk through a full domain WHOIS and DNS OSINT investigation.

WHOIS: whois target.com for registrant info, then historic WHOIS via ViewDNS.info or DomainTools to find old registrant emails before privacy protection. DNS: dig target.com ANY for all records, dig target.com MX for mail servers (reveals email provider), dig target.com TXT for SPF/DKIM/DMARC (reveals email security posture and third-party services). Zone transfer attempt: dig axfr target.com @ns1.target.com. Reverse DNS: for each discovered IP run host <ip> and whois <ip>. PTR records often reveal internal naming conventions. DNSDumpster.com and SecurityTrails for historical DNS changes — old A records reveal previous hosting providers. Check NS history for registrar transfers which can indicate acquisitions.

Primary resources: HaveIBeenPwned API (hibp-integration or curl 'https://haveibeenpwned.com/api/v3/breachedaccount/{email}'). What is certificate transparency and how do you use it for OSINT?

Certificate transparency (CT) is a public log of all SSL/TLS certificates issued. Every certificate must be logged in CT logs to be trusted. This exposes internal infrastructure that wasn't intended to be public. Query via: crt.sh — 'https://crt.sh/?q=%.target.com&output=json', Censys certificates search, Facebook CT monitor. What you find: internal subdomains (vpn.target.com, dev.target.com, staging.target.com), cloud infrastructure (app.target.com.s3.amazonaws.com), acquisitions (subsidiary domains in same cert), wildcard scope (*. internal.target.com). Automate: subfinder uses CT logs natively. Monitor for new certs on targets using certstream.

How do you build a complete target profile using Maltego?

Maltego is a visual link analysis tool with transforms. Workflow: 1) Start with domain entity, run DNS transforms to get subdomains/IPs. 2) Run Whois transforms to get registrant data. 3) Add email entities from registrant data, run Have I Been Pwned and Pipl transforms. 4) Use Shodan transform on discovered IPs for open services. 5) Social Links Community transforms for social media mapping. 6) Run PGP Key transforms to find associated email addresses. 7) Use FullContact for personal profile enrichment. 8) PhoneBook.cz transform on emails for breach data. 9) Build a complete graph: domain → IPs → employees → social profiles → breach data. Export graph as CSV for further analysis. Use Maltego CaseFile (offline) for sensitive investigations.

SpiderFoot is an automated OSINT platform that runs 200+ modules against a target. Deployment: spiderfoot -l 127.0.0.1:5001 launches web UI. CLI: spiderfoot -s target.com -m all -o json -q. Multi-vector approach: 1) EXIF data: download images before they're stripped, run exiftool — Instagram strips GPS but older Android phones sometimes bypass. 2) Timeline reconstruction: correlate post times with local events, sports results, weather mentions. 3) Language patterns: regional slang, spelling variants narrow geographic area. 4) Background analysis: building styles, vegetation, vehicle license plate formats, electrical infrastructure type. 5) Check-in history: Facebook Places, Foursquare/Swarm, Instagram location tags (even neighborhood tags narrow to city block). 6) Cross-platform correlation: same username across platforms may have location enabled on one. 7) Network connections: tagged photos by others who have public location data. 8) IP-based geolocation from email headers if target ever emailed you. What is the theHarvester tool and give a complete usage guide.

What are the best passive DNS tools and why is passive DNS valuable?

Passive DNS stores historical DNS resolution data — it shows what IPs a domain resolved to in the past and what domains have resolved to a given IP. Tools: SecurityTrails (securitytrails.com/list/ip/<ip>) — best free tier, shows complete DNS history. RiskIQ PassiveTotal — premium, comprehensive. DNSDB (Farsight Security) — largest passive DNS database. VirusTotal /domain/<domain>/resolutions — free API. CIRCL passive DNS — free, comprehensive. Value: 1) Discover old infrastructure that was decommissioned but IP still accessible. 2) Find shared hosting neighbors (multiple targets on same server). 3) Track attacker infrastructure that changed IPs — look for patterns in bulletproof hosting ASNs. 4) Attribute malware C2 to threat actor by correlating with known IOCs. 5) Discover CDN bypass — find origin IP behind Cloudflare by checking historical A records before CDN was added.

What is HUMINT in a cyber context and how is it used?

HUMINT (Human Intelligence) in cyber operations involves manipulating real people to extract intelligence or access. Digital HUMINT vectors: 1) Social Engineering — calling helpdesk as new employee to get password resets. 2) LinkedIn persona building — create convincing profile, connect with targets, gradually extract infrastructure info through 'professional' conversation. 3) Phishing with personalization — OSINT-derived spearphishing using target's hobbies, colleagues' names, current projects. 4) Watering hole — compromise sites frequented by target community. 5) Fake job posting — post job ad targeting specific skills at target company, collect resumes with personal data. 6) Conference/event networking — in-person or virtual events for direct access. HUMINT + OSINT pipeline: build target profile via OSINT → craft targeted social engineering pretext → execute HUMINT operation → extract credentials/access/intelligence.

Explain how to use OSINT to map an organization's attack surface.

How do you perform image OSINT including reverse image search and EXIF analysis?

Explain DNS enumeration techniques beyond basic queries.

Advanced DNS recon: 1) Zone transfer: dig axfr target.com @ns1.target.com — often misconfigured on internal DNS. 2) DNSSEC walking: for signed zones, enumerate all records using NSEC3 hash cracking. 3) DNS brute force: fierce -dns target.com, dnsx -d target.com -w subdomains.txt -r 100. 4) Reverse DNS sweep: for a /24 block: for i in $(seq 1 254); do host 192.168.1.$i; done. 5) DNS over HTTPS (DoH): query Cloudflare/Google DoH to bypass local DNS filtering. 6) DNS cache snooping: query a recursive resolver to check if it has cached entries for target — reveals browsing patterns. 7) Wildcard detection: if *.target.com resolves, filter out these false positives. 8) CNAME chain analysis: follow CNAME records to discover cloud services, CDNs, and potential CNAME takeover opportunities. 9) CAA records: reveal which CAs can issue certs for the domain — useful for cert issuance attack research.

How do you extract intelligence from leaked databases?

Processing: download breach dump → decompress → identify format (SQL dump, CSV, JSON). For SQL dumps: mysql -u root < dump.sql then query SELECT email,password FROM users WHERE email LIKE '%target.com%'. For large files: grep -i '@target.com' dump.csv to filter relevant records. Password analysis: use Hashcat against identified hashes — MD5/SHA1 crack in seconds with rainbow tables, bcrypt requires GPU cluster. Pattern analysis: extract all plaintext passwords from breach, analyze with PACK (Password Analysis and Cracking Toolkit) for rules and masks. Pivot: found password 'Company2019!' — try variations: Company2020!, Company2021!, Company@2024. Credential stuffing: use Snipr or Sentry MBA against target login portals. OSINT value: even old/cracked passwords reveal password policies, naming conventions, and reuse patterns. Tool: pwndb (automated breach search by email domain).

What is SIGINT in digital intelligence and how is it applied?

SIGINT (Signals Intelligence) in cyber contexts involves intercepting and analyzing electronic communications. Digital SIGINT techniques: 1) Passive WiFi monitoring: airmon-ng to capture probe requests — devices broadcast previous network SSIDs, revealing travel history and home/work network names. 2) Bluetooth enumeration: hcitool scan + btlejack for BLE advertising packets — reveals nearby device names and types. 3) RF SIGINT: HackRF One + GNU Radio for capturing and analyzing wireless communications, remote controls, tire pressure sensors (TPMS leaks vehicle and driver info). 4) Network traffic analysis: Wireshark on public WiFi captures cleartext protocols, DNS queries reveal browsing behavior even with HTTPS. 5) IMSI catching: IMSI catchers (Stingray) force phones to connect, revealing IMSI numbers and enabling tracking. 6) SDR-based reception: RTL-SDR for ADS-B (aircraft tracking), AIS (ship tracking), ACARS (aircraft communications).
